newsitem.title: UK: IATA airlines fear Hong Kong may lose traffic.
newsitem.headline: IATA airlines fear Hong Kong may lose traffic.

text.p: Airlines fear Hong Kong will lose traffic if the growing rumours surrounding a tariff-setting process are correct, an IATA statement said.

According to IATA airlines, cargo operators, business organisations and those in the tourism industry are becoming increasingly anxious concerning the lack of news on the charges that airlines may be asked to pay for using the new Hong Kong airport, Chek Lap Kok.
They fear that Hong Kong could lose one million passengers a year, said the statement.
The airlines are urging the Hong Kong airport Authority to take several points into account when proposing the new charges.
They are asking that the 'windfall' revenues of HKD 280 billion from the re-development of Kai Tak should be used to offset the costs of Chek Lap Kok.

Also the airlines are urging the Hong Kong government to review the intended five percent real rate of return on the Chek Lap Kok investment and allow the Airport Authority to retain the revenues currently collected as an airport departure tax, IATA stated.
The government should also make a full Economic Impact Study to clarify the vital contribution of Chek Lap Kok to Hong Kong's economy, IATA said.
Plans for a more aggressive commercial trading strategy, including tax-exempt retailing and duty-free sales should be drawn up, the airline body added.
Consultations between the Hong Kong Airport Authority and the airlines are set to resume on March 13.
"IATA airlines look forward to an adequate discussion and a sensible resolution of all these major issues," said the statement. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 543 7706 Fax:5017
